Make paper: 3 sugar cane in a row on a crafting table gives 3 paper.
Get leather: cows drop 0-2, horses, donkeys, mules, llamas and hoglins also drop it; Looting raises the drop count.
Craft the book: 3 paper + 1 leather (shapeless).
Turn books into bookshelves: 3 books + 6 planks of any wood gives 1 bookshelf.
Build the enchanting corner: 15 bookshelves placed around an enchanting table with a one-block air gap unlock level-30 enchantments.

Alternative sources: break existing bookshelves for 3 books each (no Silk Touch), loot village and stronghold libraries, disenchant enchanted books on a grindstone, or take gifted books from librarian villagers in Java.
editionNote: Same recipes in Java and Bedrock. In Java, librarian villagers throw books at players with the Hero of the Village effect.
versions: Books since Java Alpha 1.0.11; current 3 paper + 1 leather recipe since Beta 1.3.

faq.q: How many bookshelves do I need for max enchants?
faq.a: Exactly 15, placed around the enchanting table with one block of air between the table and the shelves. More than 15 adds nothing.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to farm books?
faq.a: An automatic or manual sugar cane farm plus a cow breeder: each book needs 3 paper and 1 leather. Raiding a stronghold library is a good one-time haul - mine the shelves without Silk Touch for 3 books each.

faq.q: Can I get leather without killing cows?
faq.a: Yes: fishing can yield leather as junk, hoglins and foxes drop it, and leatherworker villagers sell leather. But a small cow pen is by far the fastest renewable source.

keywords: book minecraft craft paper leather sugar cane bookshelf enchanting table 15 bookshelves

name: How to Make a Shield in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a shield with 6 planks of any wood and 1 iron ingot in a Y shape. Hold Use in Java or sneak in Bedrock to block frontal melee hits, arrows and explosions - but an axe or warden hit disables it for 5 seconds.
steps: Get iron: mine iron ore (or deepslate iron ore) and smelt it in a furnace or blast furnace - you only need 1 iron ingot.
Chop any tree and craft 6 planks; mixing wood types is fine.
Arrange the recipe in a Y: top row planks - iron ingot - planks, middle row planks - planks - planks, one plank in the bottom center. Out comes the shield.
Equip it in your off-hand slot so you can keep a sword, axe or tool in the main hand.
Raise the shield: hold Use (right click) in Java, or sneak in Bedrock. Blocking starts after 0.25 seconds and slows you to sneaking pace.
What it stops: frontal melee attacks, arrows, tridents and most projectiles deal no damage, and explosion knockback is reduced. Attacks of 3 damage or more wear the shield down by that amount.
Respect axes and wardens: a hit from an axe-wielding player or mob, or a warden, disables the shield for 5 seconds - back off until it recovers.

Repair and decorate: combine two damaged shields in a crafting grid to add their durability plus 5%, or craft the shield together with a banner to apply its pattern (the banner is consumed and can't be washed off).
materials: Optional: a banner to decorate it
Optional: a second shield to repair it
editionNote: Java blocks by holding Use, Bedrock by sneaking, and Bedrock knocks attackers back on a blocked melee hit. In Java, slimes, magma cubes and blazes drain shield durability fast on contact; in Bedrock you can attack while the shield is up, but attacking lowers it.
versions: Shields added in Java 1.9 (replacing sword blocking) and in Bedrock 1.10.0; the wool-based snapshot recipe only existed during Java snapshots 15w33c-15w34c.

faq.q: Can an axe break my shield?
faq.a: An axe hit does not break it - it disables the shield for 5 seconds, leaving you open. The shield itself has 336 durability and only loses it from blocked attacks of 3 or more damage.

faq.q: How do I put a banner on a shield?
faq.a: Craft the shield together with a matching banner. The banner is consumed, the shield must have no existing pattern, and unlike banners, a decorated shield cannot be washed clean in a cauldron.

faq.q: Does a shield block everything?
faq.a: No. It blocks frontal melee and non-piercing projectiles, but guardian lasers only partially, warden sonic attacks and piercing crossbow shots go through, and axes or warden melee hits disable it.

keywords: shield minecraft craft planks iron ingot block axe disable banner off hand durability 336

name: How to Make Paper in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft paper with 3 sugar cane in a row on a crafting table - that yields 3 paper. Sugar cane grows on dirt, sand or grass next to water, and you need paper for books, maps, firework rockets and name tags.
steps: Find sugar cane: it generates on riverbanks, lake shores and beaches, up to 4 blocks tall next to water.
Plant it on dirt, sand, grass or mud directly beside a water block. It grows up to 3 blocks tall on its own.
Harvest the top two blocks and leave the bottom one planted so it regrows - an early sugar cane row pays off all game.
Craft the paper: place 3 sugar cane in a horizontal row on a crafting table to get 3 paper.
Spend it well: 3 paper + 1 leather makes a book, paper + a compass makes an empty map, and paper goes into firework rockets, cartography tables, banner patterns and name tags.
Zoom maps cheaply: combining a map with paper in a cartography table zooms it out one level, about 8 times more paper-efficient than the crafting table recipe.
No cane nearby? Paper also appears in shipwreck chests and stronghold library chests, and in Java cartographer villagers gift paper to players with the Hero of the Village effect.
materials: Water-adjacent dirt, sand or grass to replant the cane
editionNote: Same crafting in Java and Bedrock. In Bedrock, paper in a cartography table can also create empty maps and empty locator maps; in Java, cartographer villagers throw paper at players with Hero of the Village.
versions: Paper since Java Alpha v1.0.11; trading paper to librarian villagers since 1.3.1 and to cartographers since 1.11.

faq.q: What is paper used for in Minecraft?
faq.a: Books (and therefore bookshelves and enchanting), maps, cartography tables, firework rockets, banner patterns and - since 1.21.6 - name tags. It also zooms maps out in a cartography table.

faq.q: Can I sell paper to villagers?
faq.a: Yes. Librarian villagers buy paper for emeralds, and cartographers buy it as their tier-1 trade, so a big sugar cane farm doubles as an emerald printer.

faq.q: Does sugar cane need light to grow?
faq.a: No light requirement matters for practical farming: plant it next to water on dirt, sand or grass and it grows on its own - harvest the top two blocks and let the bottom regrow.

keywords: paper minecraft craft sugar cane books maps cartography table firework rockets librarian trade

name: How to Get XP Fast in Minecraft
quickAnswer: The fastest XP combines a mob farm with furnace banks: common hostile mobs drop 5 XP each, smelting stores XP inside the furnace for one big payout, and quartz mining pays 2-5 XP per ore. Level 30 costs 1,395 XP total and unlocks max-level enchanting.
steps: Hunt hostile mobs: zombies, skeletons, creepers and most hostiles drop 5 XP (plus 1-3 per piece of spawned equipment) as long as they die within 5 seconds of a player hit - fall damage and fire still count if you tagged them.
Mine the right ores: nether quartz pays 2-5 XP per ore, diamond and emerald 3-7, and coal, redstone and lapis smaller amounts. Silk Touch banks the XP inside the ore block for later.

Build a furnace bank: XP from smelting stays stored in the furnace. Smelt cactus (the best payer in Java), food or cobblestone with a hopper unloading it, then take one item from the GUI to collect the entire stored pile at once.
Farm a monster spawner: a dungeon spawner feeding a kill chamber gives steady XP and drops; mining the spawner itself is a one-time 15-43 XP, so cage it, don't break it.
Use a sculk catalyst: mobs dying near sculk convert into sculk blocks that store their XP - mine the sculk to collect it. A catalyst over a mob farm is a passive XP battery.
Collect the quiet sources: trading with villagers, breeding animals, reeling in fish, bottles o' enchanting, disenchanting gear in a grindstone, and challenge advancements in Java all pay XP.
Late game jackpots: the ender dragon drops 12,000 XP the first time (500 when respawned), the wither drops 50, and raid waves with Hero of the Village farms scale even higher.
Spend it at 30: max-level enchanting needs 30 levels (1,395 XP from 0); anvils accept jobs up to level 39. On death you drop 7 XP per level, capped at 100 points - bank levels before risky trips.
materials: A sword (Looting III for drops, XP unaffected)
Furnaces plus fuel for the smelting bank
Torches and food for mining trips
Optional: Silk Touch pickaxe to bank ore XP
editionNote: Core XP sources are shared. In Java, challenge advancements pay XP and cactus is the best smelting payout; in Bedrock, smelting payouts differ slightly. Dying drops 7 XP per level up to 100 points unless keepInventory is on.
versions: Current for the latest Java and Bedrock releases; the ender dragon's first-kill payout is 12,000 XP, the highest single source in the game.

faq.q: How much XP do I need for level 30?
faq.a: 1,395 experience points from level 0. Levels cost more as they climb: the jump from 27 to 30 alone costs 306, so grind after big expenses, not before.

faq.q: What gives the most XP in Minecraft?
faq.a: The first ender dragon kill: 12,000 XP. After that, mob spawner farms, sculk catalyst setups and furnace banks give the best sustained rates, with nether quartz mining as the best casual option.

faq.q: Do I lose my XP when I die?
faq.a: You drop orbs worth 7 XP per level, capped at 100 points (roughly 7 levels), and the rest vanishes. With the keepInventory gamerule on, you keep everything.

keywords: xp fast minecraft experience farm level 30 enchanting 1395 furnace bank sculk catalyst spawner quartz

name: How to Make a Brewing Stand in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a brewing stand with 1 blaze rod in the center slot and 3 stone-tier blocks (cobblestone, blackstone or cobbled deepslate, mixed if you like) across the bottom row. Then fuel it with blaze powder and brew water bottles with nether wart and ingredients.
steps: Get a blaze rod: kill blazes around a blaze spawner in a nether fortress. Each blaze drops 0-1 blaze rods (more with Looting) - bring good armor, a bow and fire resistance potions if you can.
Mine 3 stone-tier blocks: plain cobblestone is fine, and blackstone or cobbled deepslate work too, in any mix.
Craft it: blaze rod in the center of the grid, the three blocks filling the bottom row. Out comes the brewing stand.

Free alternatives: a brewing stand also generates in the basement of igloos (with a splash potion of Weakness inside) and in village churches - but you still need blaze powder to fuel it, and that only comes from blazes.
Fuel it: craft blaze powder from blaze rods (1 rod makes 2 powder). Each powder brews 20 batches, and each ingredient stage counts as one batch.
Brew: place up to 3 water bottles in the bottom slots, nether wart on top to make awkward potions, then add your effect ingredient. Every stage takes 20 seconds.
Automate it: a hopper pointing into the top feeds ingredients, a side hopper feeds bottles, and a hopper underneath extracts finished potions.
materials: To brew: water bottles, nether wart and effect ingredients
editionNote: Works identically in both editions, with one quirk: brewing stands cannot be pushed by pistons in Java, but they can in Bedrock. Hoppers interact with the stand the same way in both.
versions: Brewing stands were added in Java Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 and Bedrock 0.12.1, and have required blaze powder as fuel since Java 1.9.

faq.q: Where do I get blaze rods for a brewing stand?
faq.a: From blazes, which spawn from blaze spawners inside nether fortresses. Each blaze drops 0-1 blaze rods, and Looting raises the maximum. There is no other renewable source.

faq.q: How much blaze powder does brewing use?
faq.a: One blaze powder fuels 20 batches. Filling all three bottle slots still counts as one batch per ingredient stage, so a single powder stretches a long way.

faq.q: Can I get a brewing stand without going to the Nether?
faq.a: You can pick one up from an igloo basement or a village church, but brewing itself needs blaze powder fuel - and blaze powder only comes from blazes. A Nether trip is unavoidable for real brewing.

keywords: brewing stand minecraft craft blaze rod cobblestone potions blaze powder awkward potion nether wart alchemy

name: How to Make a Bookshelf in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a bookshelf with 6 planks and 3 books: books across the middle row, planks filling the top and bottom rows. For maximum level 30 enchantments you need 15 bookshelves around the enchanting table - 45 books and 90 planks in total.
steps: Make books first: each book needs 3 paper and 1 leather. Paper comes from sugar cane (3 cane craft into 3 paper) and leather from cows, horses or llamas.
Chop any tree for 6 planks per shelf; mixing wood types is fine.
Craft the shelf: top row planks - planks - planks, middle row book - book - book, bottom row planks again.
Plan the full enchanting setup: 15 bookshelves cost 45 books (135 paper, so 135 sugar cane, plus 45 leather) and 90 planks.

Place them right: a ring of 15 shelves around the enchanting table, one block of air between shelf and table, at the table's level or one block higher. Anything solid in the gap (even a torch or carpet) blocks that shelf.
Move them safely: a bookshelf drops only its 3 books when broken, so mine them with a Silk Touch tool if you want the shelf itself back.
Free shelves: village libraries, stronghold libraries (161-233 shelves each) and woodland mansion rooms are full of bookshelves ready to loot.
materials: Optional: Silk Touch tool to move shelves whole
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock. Note that the chiseled bookshelf added in 1.20 stores books and works with comparators, but does NOT raise enchantment levels - only the classic bookshelf does.
versions: Bookshelves were added in Java 0.26 SURVIVAL TEST and Bedrock 0.2.0; the maximum enchanting setup was reduced from 30 to 15 bookshelves in Java 1.3.

faq.q: How many bookshelves do I need for level 30 enchantments?
faq.a: Exactly 15, placed in a ring around the enchanting table with one air block between shelf and table. More than 15 adds nothing.

faq.q: Do chiseled bookshelves work for enchanting?
faq.a: No. Chiseled bookshelves (added in 1.20) store books and emit comparator signals, but only the classic bookshelf boosts the enchanting table.

faq.q: Why did my bookshelf drop books instead of the block?
faq.a: That is the normal drop: 3 books. To get the bookshelf block itself, mine it with a Silk Touch enchanted tool.

keywords: bookshelf minecraft craft planks books enchanting table level 30 15 bookshelves silk touch sugar cane leather

name: How to Make a Piston in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a piston with 3 planks across the top row, 4 cobblestone down the sides, 1 iron ingot in the center and 1 redstone dust under it. Combine the finished piston with a slimeball to get a sticky piston that also pulls blocks back.
steps: Gather the materials: 3 planks of any wood, 4 cobblestone, 1 iron ingot and 1 redstone dust.
Get redstone: mine redstone ore deep underground (it generates below Y 16, densest around Y -59) with an iron pickaxe or better; each ore drops 4-5 redstone dust.
Craft the piston: top row planks - planks - planks, middle row cobblestone - iron ingot - cobblestone, bottom row cobblestone - redstone dust - cobblestone.
Make it sticky: put the piston in a grid with a slimeball on top. Slimeballs come from slimes, which spawn in swamps at night and in slime chunks below Y 40 - or from baby pandas sneezing.
Know the limits: a piston pushes up to 12 blocks, but obsidian, bedrock, extended piston heads and (in Java) block entities like chests and furnaces will not move.
Power it: any redstone signal works - a lever, button, pressure plate, redstone torch or a powered block next to the piston. The head extends toward whatever it faces when placed.
editionNote: In Bedrock, pistons can push block entities such as chests, furnaces and brewing stands; in Java they cannot. One-tick pulses make a sticky piston drop its block instead of pulling it, with slightly different timing behavior between editions.
versions: Pistons were added in Java Beta 1.7 and Bedrock 0.15.0, and sticky pistons alongside them.

faq.q: What is the difference between a piston and a sticky piston?
faq.a: A normal piston only pushes blocks; when the power turns off, the blocks stay where they are. A sticky piston (piston + slimeball) also pulls one block back when it retracts.

faq.q: Why won't my piston push a chest or furnace?
faq.a: In Java, block entities like chests, furnaces and brewing stands are immovable. In Bedrock they can be pushed, so the same machine may only work in one edition.

faq.q: How many blocks can one piston move?
faq.a: Up to 12 blocks in a line, counting everything the push chain touches. If the chain exceeds 12 or hits an immovable block, the piston does not extend.

keywords: piston minecraft craft sticky piston slimeball redstone planks cobblestone iron push 12 blocks

name: How to Make an Anvil in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft an anvil with 3 blocks of iron across the top row, 1 iron ingot in the center and 3 iron ingots along the bottom - 31 iron ingots in total. Use it to repair gear, combine enchantments and rename items, but each use has a 12% chance to degrade it: chipped, then damaged, then it breaks.
steps: Smelt 31 iron ingots - just under half a stack. Mining plus a furnace does it; an iron farm makes it trivial.
Craft 3 blocks of iron by filling the grid with ingots (9 each, 27 of the 31).
Craft the anvil: top row block of iron - block of iron - block of iron, iron ingot in the center slot, bottom row ingot - ingot - ingot.
Rename anything: put any item in the first slot and type the new name - 1 experience level plus any prior work penalty.
Repair with materials: an iron pickaxe repaired with iron ingots regains 25% of its max durability per ingot, enchantments intact.
Combine enchantments: merge two enchanted items (or item + enchanted book) to stack or transfer enchantments - two Sharpness II swords become Sharpness III.
Watch the costs: the prior work penalty doubles every time the same item goes through an anvil, and in survival the anvil refuses any job costing 40 levels or more.

Expect it to die: each use has a 12% chance to degrade the anvil (chipped, damaged, destroyed), about 25 uses on average. Falls damage it too - and an anvil landing on a mob or player deals 2 damage per block fallen, up to 40.
editionNote: Identical mechanics in both editions. Details differ only in renaming: up to 50 characters in Java, 30 in Bedrock, and Bedrock names support section-sign formatting codes.
versions: Anvils were added in Java 1.4.2 (12w41a) and Bedrock 0.12.1, in all three damage states.

faq.q: Why does my anvil say Too Expensive?
faq.a: In survival, anvil jobs are capped at 39 levels. The prior work penalty doubles each time an item goes through the anvil, so heavy gear eventually becomes unfixable - combine books onto the item in the cheapest order, or disenchant with a grindstone and start over.

faq.q: Can you repair an anvil?
faq.a: No. A chipped or damaged anvil cannot be fixed - when it breaks you craft a new one. It survives about 25 uses on average.

faq.q: Is there a free anvil anywhere?
faq.a: A damaged anvil generates in the forge room of woodland mansions and inside trail ruins, ready to loot with any pickaxe.

keywords: anvil minecraft craft 31 iron ingots blocks of iron repair rename combine enchantments too expensive prior work

name: How to Make TNT in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft TNT with 5 gunpowder and 4 sand (or red sand) in a checkerboard: gunpowder in the corners and center, sand on the sides. Prime it with flint and steel, redstone or another explosion and it flashes for 4 seconds before blowing up with power 4.
steps: Farm gunpowder: creepers drop 0-2 (more with Looting) when killed by a player - hunt them at night or build a creeper farm. Ghasts and witches drop it too.
Dig 4 sand blocks; red sand works exactly the same.
Craft in a checkerboard: gunpowder in the four corners and the center, sand in the middle of each edge.
Prime it: use flint and steel, a redstone signal, fire, a flaming arrow or a nearby explosion. The block becomes a falling entity that flashes white and explodes after 80 ticks (4 seconds).
Use the physics: primed TNT falls, and flowing water, pistons and other explosions push it - the working principle of every TNT cannon.
Mine with it: since Java 1.14, blocks destroyed by TNT always drop their items. TNT clears netherrack fast while blast-resistant ancient debris survives - the classic netherite mining method.

Know the limits: obsidian, bedrock and ancient debris resist it, and TNT normally cannot destroy blocks underwater (entities still take damage). In Java, a falling block like sand landing inside the primed TNT lets it break blocks underwater; in Bedrock there is no workaround.
materials: To prime: flint and steel or a redstone signal
editionNote: Underwater block-breaking tricks (sand falling into primed TNT, bubble columns) only work in Java; in Bedrock, TNT never destroys blocks underwater - only the Education-edition Underwater TNT variant does.
versions: TNT was added in Java 0.26 SURVIVAL TEST and Pocket Edition 0.1.0, the fuse has been 4 seconds since early 2010, and destroyed blocks have always dropped items since Java 1.14.

faq.q: How do I get gunpowder for TNT?
faq.a: Creepers are the renewable source: 0-2 gunpowder per kill, up to 5 with Looting III. A basic dark-room creeper farm produces stacks per hour. Ghasts and witches drop it too, but far less reliably.

faq.q: Does TNT destroy obsidian or ancient debris?
faq.a: No. TNT explodes with power 4, and obsidian, bedrock, crying obsidian and ancient debris have far higher blast resistance - which is exactly why TNT mining exposes ancient debris instead of destroying it.

faq.q: Can I make TNT explode instantly?
faq.a: A TNT minecart (TNT + minecart) explodes instantly on an activator rail, a hard crash or fire. Normal primed TNT always takes 4 seconds.

keywords: tnt minecraft craft gunpowder sand creeper explosion flint and steel tnt cannon mining ancient debris

name: How to Respawn the Ender Dragon in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place 4 end crystals on the edges of the exit portal, one per side, after killing the ender dragon. A 30-second sequence resets the obsidian pillars and their crystals, then the dragon returns - worth 500 XP per rematch instead of the 12,000 from the first kill.
steps: Kill the ender dragon first - respawning only works after the original fight is won.
Craft 4 end crystals: each needs 7 glass, 1 eye of ender and 1 ghast tear, so 28 glass, 4 eyes and 4 tears in total.
Go back to the exit portal, the bedrock fountain at the center of the End's main island.
Place one end crystal on the middle block of each of the portal's four edges - they snap onto the bedrock.

Stand back: the four crystals shoot beams at every pillar, explosions reset the obsidian pillars, iron bars and end crystals, and after about 30 seconds the dragon spawns at (0, 128, 0). The four summoning crystals then explode.
Do not break any of the four crystals during the sequence - that cancels the summoning. The pillar crystals are invulnerable while it runs.

Collect the rewards: 500 XP per respawned dragon, fresh end crystals to farm, and a new end gateway per kill, up to 20 gateways. Collect the dragon egg first - it vanishes if you respawn the dragon before picking it up.
materials: 4 end crystals (each: 7 glass + 1 eye of ender + 1 ghast tear)
Total: 28 glass, 4 eyes of ender, 4 ghast tears
editionNote: In Java the four crystals go on the edge blocks of the exit portal; in Bedrock they may also sit one block outward in each direction, though uneven arrangements are unreliable there.
versions: Dragon respawning was added in Java 1.9 (15w44a) and Bedrock 1.0.0; respawned dragons have dropped 500 experience since the same update.

faq.q: Do I get another dragon egg from a respawned dragon?
faq.a: No. Only the very first kill drops a dragon egg - and if you respawn the dragon without collecting it, the egg disappears forever.

faq.q: How much XP does a respawned dragon give?
faq.a: 500 experience points, down from 12,000 for the first kill. It is still one of the fastest XP sources per minute in the game.

faq.q: How many times can I respawn the ender dragon?
faq.a: Unlimited times, as long as you keep crafting end crystals. Each kill - original or rematch - generates one end gateway, up to a maximum of 20.

keywords: respawn ender dragon minecraft 4 end crystals exit portal 500 xp dragon egg ghast tear rematch

name: How to Make a Snow Golem in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Stack 2 snow blocks vertically and place a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern on top - the snow golem comes alive instantly. It throws snowballs at monsters (1 per second, damage only to blazes) and leaves a trail of snow, but it melts in hot biomes and rain unless it has Fire Resistance.
steps: Gather snow: dig snow layers with a shovel (a Silk Touch shovel drops snow blocks directly). Craft 4 snowballs into a snow block - you need 2 blocks, so 8 snowballs.
Get a carved pumpkin: place any pumpkin and use shears on it to carve the face, or craft a jack o'lantern (carved pumpkin + torch) - both work as the head.
Build it: place the 2 snow blocks in a vertical stack, then put the carved pumpkin on top. The pattern also works sideways or upside-down, as long as the pumpkin goes last.

Know its weapon: the golem moves toward monsters and pelts them with snowballs from up to 10 blocks away (16 when confined), one per second. Snowballs only damage blazes (3 per hit) but knock back everything else - a distraction, not a defender.
Farm snow with it: the golem leaves a snow layer trail wherever it walks (in Java, in any biome since 1.18). Trap one on a small platform and dig the trail for unlimited snowballs.
Keep it alive: it takes damage in rain, in water and in biomes hotter than 1.0 (deserts, savannas, badlands, the Nether). A splash potion of Fire Resistance lets it survive even the Nether.
Shear it for fun: use shears on the golem to remove the pumpkin (it drops as an item) and reveal its derpy snowman face underneath.
materials: 1 carved pumpkin (carve any pumpkin with shears) or 1 jack o'lantern
editionNote: The snow trail works in every biome in Java (since 1.18), but in Bedrock hot biomes like jungles, savannas, deserts and the Nether block the trail. Fire Resistance protects the golem from heat damage in both.
versions: Snow golems were added in Java Beta 1.9 Prerelease (1.0.0) and Pocket Edition 0.12.0, and jack o'lantern heads have worked from the start.

faq.q: Why did my snow golem die in the desert or the Nether?
faq.a: Biomes with a temperature above 1.0 (deserts, savannas, badlands and every Nether biome) melt it, and rain or water hurts it too. Give it a splash potion of Fire Resistance to make it heat-proof.

faq.q: Do snow golem snowballs deal damage?
faq.a: Only to blazes: 3 damage per hit, which makes snow golems a cheap blaze farm helper. Against everything else the snowballs just knock mobs back - and provoke them to attack the golem.

faq.q: How do I use a snow golem as a snow farm?
faq.a: Trap the golem in a 1x1 space with a roof, then dig the snow layer trail it leaves under itself with a shovel. The trail regenerates instantly, giving unlimited snowballs.

keywords: snow golem minecraft build snow blocks carved pumpkin snowballs snow farm melt fire resistance blaze

name: How to Make an Ender Chest in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft an ender chest with 8 obsidian in a ring around 1 eye of ender. Its 27 slots follow you across every ender chest in the world and between dimensions - each player sees their own inventory, even on servers.
steps: Mine 8 obsidian with a diamond or netherite pickaxe - pour water over lava source blocks to make it, or loot ruined portals.
Craft an eye of ender: blaze powder (from blaze rods) plus an ender pearl (from endermen or bartering with piglins).
Craft the chest: fill every slot with obsidian except the center, which takes the eye of ender.
Use it like a normal chest with a twist: the contents are stored per player and shared across every ender chest in every dimension, so what you put in at home is waiting for you in the End.
Put your backup kit inside: valuables stored in an ender chest survive your death completely - nobody else can see or steal them, even in multiplayer.
Mine it back with Silk Touch: without Silk Touch an ender chest drops only 8 obsidian and the eye of ender is lost. A Silk Touch pickaxe drops the chest itself.
Pair it with a shulker box for the classic explorer loadout: the shulker box stays in the ender chest, so your whole camp fits in one slot of your always-available storage.
materials: 1 eye of ender (blaze powder + ender pearl)
Diamond or netherite pickaxe to mine the obsidian
Silk Touch pickaxe to move the chest afterwards
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock: the inventory is per player and synced across dimensions in both, and both need Silk Touch to drop the chest itself.
versions: Ender chests were added in Java 1.3.1 (12w21a) and Bedrock 1.0.0.

faq.q: Can other players open my ender chest?
faq.a: They can open the block, but they see their own inventory, never yours. Every player has a separate ender chest inventory linked to their account, so nothing inside can be stolen.

faq.q: Do ender chests work between the Overworld, Nether and End?
faq.a: Yes. The same 27 slots are available from every ender chest in every dimension - it is the only vanilla way to access your items across dimensions.

faq.q: Why did my ender chest drop obsidian instead of the chest?
faq.a: Without Silk Touch, breaking an ender chest returns the 8 obsidian but destroys the eye of ender. Always move it with a Silk Touch pickaxe.

keywords: ender chest minecraft craft obsidian eye of ender cross dimension storage silk touch per player inventory

name: How to Make a Hopper in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a hopper with 5 iron ingots in a V around 1 chest: ingots in the top-left and top-right, the middle-left and middle-right, and one ingot under the chest in the bottom center. It moves items at 2.5 per second and locks when powered by redstone.
steps: Smelt 5 iron ingots and craft 1 chest (8 planks of any wood).
Craft the hopper: iron ingot top-left, iron ingot top-right, ingot middle-left - chest middle - ingot middle-right, and one ingot below the chest in the bottom center.

Aim it on placement: the little tube at the bottom points where items go. Sneak while placing to attach it to the face of a chest, furnace or other container - the tube faces whatever face you clicked.
Let it work: a hopper pushes items into the container it faces, pulls from the container above, and collects loose item drops floating over it - 1 item every 0.4 seconds, so 2.5 items per second.
Automate furnaces: hopper on top feeds fuel or input, hopper on the side feeds the other slot, hopper underneath extracts the result. Same trick for brewing stands and composters.
Lock it with redstone: any powered signal (lever, redstone torch, powered block) freezes the hopper completely until the power turns off - the standard way to pause item flow in farms.
Build hopper chains: hoppers pointing into hoppers move items horizontally over long distances; lock one hopper to stop a horizontal chain, two adjacent ones for a vertical chain.
editionNote: Core behavior is the same in both editions. Technical differences: in Bedrock a hopper can only be locked on the input redstone tick, and hopper performance tuning differs (composters on top help in Java, hurt in Bedrock).
versions: Hoppers were added in Java 1.5 (13w01a) and Bedrock 0.14.0.

faq.q: How fast is a hopper?
faq.a: One item every 8 game ticks: 0.4 seconds per item, or 2.5 items per second (9,000 per hour). A single hopper line can bottleneck big farms - split the flow across several hoppers.

faq.q: Why won't my hopper feed the chest next to it?
faq.a: The hopper only pushes into the block its tube points at. If you placed it without sneaking, it probably points down instead of sideways - break it, then sneak-click the side face of the chest.

faq.q: How do I stop a hopper from moving items?
faq.a: Power it with redstone. A locked hopper stops pushing, pulling and collecting, though other hoppers can still push into it or pull out of it - so vertical chains need two adjacent hoppers locked at once.

keywords: hopper minecraft craft 5 iron chest automation item transfer 2.5 items per second redstone lock furnace farm

name: How to Make a Bed in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a bed with 3 matching wool in a row over 3 planks of any wood. Sleep at night (or during a thunderstorm) to skip to morning and set your respawn point - but never try to sleep in the Nether or the End: the bed explodes with more power than TNT.
steps: Get 3 wool of the same color: shear sheep (1-3 wool each, and they regrow it) or kill them for 1. All three pieces must match - mixed colors do not craft.
Chop any tree for 3 planks; mixing wood types is fine.
Craft it: the 3 matching wool filling the middle row, the 3 planks filling the bottom row. The bed takes the wool's color.
Sleep at night: use the bed when it gets dark (or during a thunderstorm, at any hour). After about 5 seconds it is morning, rain and snow stop, and phantoms reset.
Set your respawn: a successful sleep sets your spawn point to the bed. If the bed is later broken or blocked, you respawn at world spawn instead.
Keep monsters away: you cannot sleep if a hostile mob is within 8 blocks horizontally and 5 vertically of the bed head - light up and secure the room first.
NEVER in the Nether or the End: using a bed there makes it explode with power 5 (stronger than TNT's 4) and sets everything on fire. In the Nether, use a respawn anchor instead.
Help villagers too: villagers sleep in beds at night and need spare beds to breed - a bed is the core of any villager breeder or village.
editionNote: Works the same in both editions, explosions included - in Bedrock you can disable bed explosions with the respawnBlocksExplode gamerule. One Bedrock quirk: waterlogged beds need Water Breathing or Conduit Power to sleep in.
versions: Beds were added in Java Beta 1.3 and Pocket Edition 0.4.0 - all red at first; the 16 colors arrived in Java 1.12. The straw bed variant arrived in 26.10.

faq.q: Why does my bed explode in the Nether?
faq.a: Intentional game design: beds only work in the Overworld. Using one in the Nether, the End or a disabled custom dimension detonates it with explosion power 5 and sets fires. Use a respawn anchor (crying obsidian + glowstone) to set a Nether spawn point.

faq.q: Why can't I sleep - 'monsters nearby'?
faq.a: A hostile mob is within 8 blocks horizontally and 5 vertically of the bed's head, even through walls. Kill it or move the bed; lighting the area stops new spawns.

faq.q: Does the bed color matter?
faq.a: Only cosmetically. All 16 colors work identically, and you can re-dye an existing bed with one dye instead of crafting a new one.

keywords: bed minecraft craft 3 wool planks sleep respawn point explode nether monsters nearby colors

name: How to Make a Compass in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a compass with 4 iron ingots around 1 redstone dust in a plus shape. It always points to your world spawn point; use it on a lodestone to make it point to that lodestone instead, even in the Nether or the End.
steps: Smelt 4 iron ingots and mine 1 redstone dust (redstone ore below Y 16, iron pickaxe or better).
Craft it: redstone dust in the center, iron ingots above, below, left and right - a plus shape.

Read it: the red needle always points to your world spawn point - the place you first appeared, not your bed. Hold it in your hand or watch it in the inventory; it works from anywhere in the Overworld.
In the Nether and the End a normal compass spins randomly and is useless - this is where the lodestone comes in.

Make a lodestone compass: craft or find a lodestone (1 netherite ingot + 8 chiseled stone bricks, or loot one in bastion remnants), place it, and use your compass on it. The compass now points to that lodestone forever, in any dimension.
Recover it if the lodestone breaks: a lodestone compass whose lodestone is destroyed spins randomly again until re-linked.
Know the variants: the recovery compass (compass + 8 echo shards from ancient cities) points to your last death location instead - a different item, crafted, not linked.
materials: For a lodestone compass: + 1 lodestone (1 netherite ingot + 8 chiseled stone bricks)
editionNote: Identical in both editions, lodestone linking included. The needle animation differs slightly (104 frames in Java, 28 in Bedrock) - purely cosmetic.
versions: Compasses were added in Java Alpha 1.1.0 and became functional in Pocket Edition 0.8.0; lodestone compasses arrived with lodestones in 1.16.

faq.q: Why does my compass not point to my bed?
faq.a: It never does - a compass points to world spawn, the fixed point where the world started. For a personal waypoint, link the compass to a lodestone placed at your base.

faq.q: Why does my compass spin in circles?
faq.a: Either you are in the Nether or the End, where normal compasses do not work, or your lodestone compass lost its lodestone. Link it to a lodestone in the dimension you are exploring.

faq.q: What is the difference between a compass and a recovery compass?
faq.a: The normal compass points to world spawn (or its lodestone). The recovery compass - compass plus 8 echo shards - points to where you last died, and only works for the player who died, in the same dimension.

keywords: compass minecraft craft 4 iron redstone world spawn lodestone compass nether recovery compass waypoint

name: How to Make a Fishing Rod in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a fishing rod with 3 sticks diagonally and 2 string hanging from the last one. Cast into water, watch the bobber for bubbles and a splash, then reel in - fish, junk or treasure like enchanted books, name tags and nautilus shells.
steps: Get 3 sticks (craft 2 planks into 4 sticks) and 2 string from spiders, cobwebs or cat gifts.
Craft it: sticks in a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, with one string under the middle stick and another under the top one.
Cast into any water: use the rod to throw the bobber out. Rivers, oceans, ponds, even a 1x1 water hole all work.
Wait for bubbles: a trail of bubbles swims toward the bobber - when it dips with a splash sound, reel in immediately.
Know the loot table: most catches are fish (cod, salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish), some are junk, and about 5% is treasure: enchanted books and bows, name tags, nautilus shells, saddles and more.
Enchant it: Luck of the Sea shifts the odds toward treasure, Lure cuts the waiting time, Unbreaking and Mending keep it alive forever. The rod has 64 durability in Java, 385 in Bedrock.
Hook mobs too: the rod grabs mobs and items (Java) and reels them toward you without damage - a poor man's grappling hook for pulling mobs off cliffs.
Make a carrot on a stick: craft the rod with a carrot to steer pigs (or warped fungus for striders in the Nether). When it wears out, it turns back into a fishing rod.
editionNote: Mechanics are the same, but durability differs wildly: 64 uses in Java, 385 in Bedrock. In Java the rod can hook loose item entities; in Bedrock a flaming bobber can set hooked mobs on fire.
versions: Fishing rods were added in Java Alpha 1.1.1 and Pocket Edition 0.11.0; the treasure and junk loot tables arrived in Java 1.7.2.

faq.q: What can you get from fishing in Minecraft?
faq.a: Fish (raw cod, salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish), junk (lily pads, bowls, leather, sticks...) and treasure (enchanted books, enchanted bows and rods, name tags, nautilus shells, saddles). Luck of the Sea nearly triples the treasure rate.

faq.q: Why is fishing so slow?
faq.a: Base wait is 5 to 30 seconds per catch. Lure III cuts it dramatically, and fishing in open water (direct sky above) is faster - rain shortens the wait too.

faq.q: Can I repair a fishing rod?
faq.a: Yes: combine two damaged rods in a crafting grid, or use an anvil. Better, put Mending on a good one and every catch repairs it with XP.

keywords: fishing rod minecraft craft 3 sticks 2 string fishing treasure enchanted book luck of the sea lure nautilus shell

name: How to Make a Map in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft an empty map with 8 paper around a compass (in Bedrock you can also use 9 paper for a map without a player marker). Hold it and use it to draw the terrain around you; zoom it out with more paper, and clone or lock it on a cartography table.
steps: Get 8 paper: craft sugar cane (3 in a row = 3 paper). You will want a sugar cane farm for this - maps eat paper.
Get 1 compass: 4 iron ingots around 1 redstone dust.
Craft the empty map: compass in the center, paper filling every other slot. In Bedrock you can skip the compass - 9 paper makes a map, but without the marker showing where you are.
Draw it: hold the empty map and use it. It fills in with a top-down view of the area around you, north always at the top.
Understand the grid: the map does NOT center on you. The world is split into invisible grid squares and your map covers whichever square you stood in when you first used it.
Explore to fill it: the map only records terrain while you hold it (either hand), in a 128-block radius around you - 64 blocks in the Nether. It only maps the surface, even underground.
Zoom it out: surround the drawn map with 8 more paper on a crafting table (or combine it with 1 paper in a cartography table) to see 4 times the area. Repeat up to 4 times for a huge regional map.
Clone and lock on a cartography table: map + empty map = two copies for friends or a wall; map + glass pane = locked, so it never updates again. Perfect for finished map-wall art.
materials: In Bedrock without a marker: 9 paper
To zoom out: + 8 paper per level, up to 4 levels
editionNote: Big difference here: Java maps always show your position marker and need a compass in the recipe. In Bedrock, only a 'locator map' (crafted with a compass) shows the marker; a map made with just paper does not. Bedrock also lets you start a new world with a free locator map via the Starting Map option.
versions: Maps were added in Java Beta 1.6 and Pocket Edition 0.14.0; the cartography table arrived with 1.14 in both editions.

faq.q: Why is my map blank or not filling in?
faq.a: An empty map only starts drawing when you hold it and press use. After that it only records while held in your hand - and only the surface within range of where you walk.

faq.q: Why is my map not centered on me?
faq.a: By design: maps snap to a fixed world grid so maps of the same zoom level never overlap. To map the neighboring area, walk past the edge of the current map and use a fresh one.

faq.q: How do I make a big map wall?
faq.a: Zoom several maps out to the same level, fill each one in a different grid square, then place them in item frames side by side - they join seamlessly. Lock them with glass panes on a cartography table once they are perfect.

keywords: map minecraft craft 8 paper compass empty map locator map zoom out cartography table clone lock map wall

name: How to Make a Bucket in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a bucket with 3 iron ingots in a V shape. It carries water, lava, milk and powder snow - and with a quick scoop you can even pick up fish, axolotls and tadpoles to move them wherever you want.
steps: Smelt 3 iron ingots (iron ore is everywhere below sea level; stone pickaxe or better).
Craft it: one ingot in the middle-left slot, one in the middle-right, one in the bottom-center - a V shape.
Scoop water: use the bucket on a water source block. Water buckets are the base of farms, elevators, obsidian casting and the classic MLG water landing.
Scoop lava the same way in caves or the Nether: fuel for 100 smelts, a trash can, or a weapon.
Milk a cow, mooshroom or goat: use the empty bucket on one. Milk clears every status effect - including bad ones like poison and the raid-triggering Bad Omen.
Pick up powder snow in snowy slopes and groves: place it to make traps, or carry it to walk on powder snow safely with leather boots.
Catch live mobs: use a water bucket on a fish, axolotl or tadpole to pick it up alive. This is the only way to move axolotls for a blue axolotl farm and tropical fish for your aquarium.
Empty it by using it again on any spot - the placed block or mob comes out, and you keep the bucket forever.
editionNote: Identical recipe and behavior in both editions. One Java quirk: using a bucket directly on a waterlogged block does not scoop it. And in the current 26.x snapshots the bucket can also carry sulfur cubes - brand new content.
versions: Buckets were added in Java Infdev on June 15, 2010 - one of the oldest items in the game - and in Pocket Edition 0.7.0.

faq.q: How do you get water in a bucket in Minecraft?
faq.a: Craft the bucket (3 iron ingots in a V), then use it on a water source block - not flowing water. Rivers, oceans and lakes are all free refills; a 2x2 hole filled with water makes an infinite source.

faq.q: Can a bucket break or run out?
faq.a: No. The bucket itself never wears out - you only lose its contents. One bucket lasts your whole world.

faq.q: How do you pick up an axolotl?
faq.a: Use a water bucket on it and it becomes a bucket of axolotl, which you can carry and release anywhere. Same trick works on cod, salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish and tadpoles.

keywords: bucket minecraft craft 3 iron ingots water bucket lava bucket milk powder snow bucket of axolotl fish infinite water

name: How to Make a Lantern in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a lantern with 8 iron nuggets around a torch. It glows at light level 15 - as bright as glowstone - and sits on top of blocks or hangs from ceilings. Swap the torch for a soul torch to get the blue soul lantern.
steps: Get 1 iron ingot and craft it into 9 iron nuggets (one ingot in any slot).
Make a torch: stick + coal or charcoal.
Craft the lantern: torch in the center, iron nuggets filling the other 8 slots.
Place it two ways: on top of a block like a little lamp, or hanging under a block like a ceiling light. If the block it hangs from is broken, the lantern breaks and drops itself.
Enjoy the light: level 15, the maximum in the game - same as glowstone, sea lanterns and shroomlights, and brighter than torches (14). It even melts snow layers within 2 blocks and ice within 3.

Make the blue variant: craft a soul torch (stick + coal + soul sand or soul soil) and surround it with nuggets for a soul lantern - spooky blue light at level 10 that piglins fear and that does not melt snow or ice.
Find them in the wild too: lanterns generate as lamps in snowy tundra villages, and soul lanterns hang in bastion remnants - or buy lanterns from apprentice librarian villagers for an emerald.
materials: For a soul lantern: 1 soul torch instead (stick + coal + soul sand/soil)
editionNote: Same in both editions since they fully arrived (Java 1.14, Bedrock 1.9 experimental and 1.10 stable). Chains look great with hanging lanterns and are crafted from nuggets too - 2 nuggets + 1 ingot.
versions: Lanterns were added in Java 1.14 (snapshot 18w46a) and Bedrock 1.9.0 behind Experimental Gameplay; soul lanterns came with the Nether Update, 1.16 in both editions.

faq.q: Are lanterns brighter than torches?
faq.a: Yes: lanterns emit light level 15, the highest possible, while torches emit 14. A lantern also melts nearby snow and ice, which torches barely do - and it simply looks better on a chain.

faq.q: How do you make a blue lantern in Minecraft?
faq.a: That is the soul lantern: same recipe but with a soul torch (stick + coal + soul sand or soul soil) in the center. It glows blue at light level 10 and piglins avoid it.

faq.q: Can lanterns hang from ceilings?
faq.a: Yes - place them against the bottom face of a block and they hang with a little ring. Combine with chains for long hanging lights. If the supporting block breaks, the lantern pops off and drops.

keywords: lantern minecraft craft 8 iron nuggets torch light level 15 hanging lantern soul lantern blue light chain

name: How to Make a Torch in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft 4 torches with 1 stick under 1 coal or charcoal. Place them on top of or against the side of blocks: they shine at light level 14 and stop monsters from spawning nearby.
steps: Get coal: mine coal ore (the black-speckled stone, everywhere from mountains to caves) with any pickaxe. No coal yet? Smelt logs in a furnace to get charcoal - it works identically.
Get sticks: craft 2 planks into 4 sticks.
Craft torches: coal or charcoal in the middle slot, stick directly below it. Each craft makes 4 torches.
Place them on the top face or the side of most solid blocks. They attach to walls too, so you can light corridors without wasting floor space.
Light up everything: a torch emits light level 14, the second brightest common light. Hostile mobs only spawn in darkness (light level 0), so a torch every 10 blocks or so keeps an area spawn-proof.
Mark your way: torches on cave walls are the classic breadcrumb trail - put them always on the same side and you will never get lost again.
Upgrade later: a torch surrounded by 8 iron nuggets becomes a lantern (light 15), and a stick + coal + soul sand or soul soil makes a soul torch with spooky blue light (level 10).

Find them for free: torches generate naturally in mineshafts, village lamp posts, strongholds, igloo basements, woodland mansions, pillager outposts and ancient cities - mine them and they drop themselves.
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock. One useful mechanic everywhere: gravity blocks like sand and gravel that fall onto a torch break and drop as items - great for clearing columns fast.
versions: Torches were added to Java in Indev 0.31 on December 23, 2009 - they are older than crafting itself - and have been in Pocket Edition since its first demo.

faq.q: How many torches do I need to stop mobs spawning?
faq.a: Mobs spawn only at block light level 0. A torch is 14 at its center and fades by 1 per block, so spacing torches about 10-12 blocks apart keeps every block above 0. Caves need more because light does not go around corners.

faq.q: Coal or charcoal - what is the difference?
faq.a: Nothing at all for torches. Charcoal is just smelted logs and behaves exactly like coal in every recipe except that it cannot be crafted into coal blocks.

faq.q: Do torches melt snow and ice?
faq.a: Only very close: they melt snow layers within 2 blocks and ice within 3. For serious melting power use a lantern (light 15), which reaches further and looks better doing it.

keywords: torch minecraft craft stick coal charcoal light level 14 stop mobs spawning spawn proof soul torch lantern

name: How to Make Shears in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft shears with 2 iron ingots in a diagonal. Use them to shear sheep for 1-3 wool without hurting them, harvest honeycomb from bee nests, carve pumpkins, and collect leaves, vines and cobwebs as blocks.
steps: Smelt 2 iron ingots - iron ore is everywhere, stone pickaxe or better.
Craft shears: one ingot in the center slot, one in the bottom-left - a diagonal. That is the whole recipe.
Shear sheep: use the shears on a sheep for 1-3 wool, no killing needed. The sheep regrows its wool after eating grass, so a sheared flock is a renewable wool factory.
Shear more mobs: mooshrooms turn into cows and drop 5 mushrooms; snow golems lose their pumpkin head and reveal their face; bogged drop their mushrooms.
Harvest honeycomb safely: place a lit campfire under a bee nest or hive, then shear it at honey level 5 for 3 honeycomb - the smoke keeps the bees calm.
Carve pumpkins: shears on a pumpkin turn it into a carved pumpkin (plus 4 pumpkin seeds) for jack o'lanterns and golem building.
Collect delicate blocks: shears harvest leaves, vines, glow lichen, cobwebs, seagrass, kelp and honeycomb blocks as items - things that otherwise drop nothing or need Silk Touch.
Watch the durability: 238 uses in Java, 239 in Bedrock. Repair by combining two pairs, or enchant with Unbreaking and Mending.
editionNote: Same recipe in both editions; durability differs by a single point (238 Java, 239 Bedrock). In Java you can also load shears into a dispenser for automatic sheep shearing farms; that automation is a Java staple.
versions: Shears were added in Java Beta 1.7 - before that, sheep had to be punched for wool - and in Pocket Edition 0.2.0.

faq.q: How do you get wool without killing sheep?
faq.a: Use shears on the sheep: 1-3 wool per shearing, and the sheep regrows its wool by eating grass. Killing a sheep only ever gives 1 wool, so shears are always better.

faq.q: How do you get honeycomb without angry bees?
faq.a: Put a lit campfire directly under the nest or hive (or a dispenser with shears facing it), then shear at honey level 5. The smoke calms the bees so they will not sting.

faq.q: Can shears get cobwebs?
faq.a: Yes - shears are the fastest way to break cobwebs and the only way to harvest them as items without Silk Touch. You will need them for mineshaft looting and string-free wool.

keywords: shears minecraft craft 2 iron ingots shear sheep wool honeycomb bee nest carve pumpkin cobwebs dispenser

name: How to Make a Smoker in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a smoker with 1 furnace surrounded by 4 logs of any wood. It cooks food twice as fast as a normal furnace - 5 seconds per item - and doubles as a butcher villager's job site block.
steps: Craft a furnace: 8 cobblestone (or blackstone/cobbled deepslate) filling every slot except the center.
Get 4 logs of any wood - any type, stripped or unstripped, even Nether stems work.
Craft the smoker: furnace in the center, one log above, below, left and right - a plus shape.
Cook food in it: raw beef, porkchops, chicken, mutton, rabbit, cod, salmon, potatoes and kelp all cook in 5 seconds instead of the furnace's 10.
Know the trade-off: fuel burns at double speed too, so each piece of coal still cooks the same 8 items - you are trading nothing, just saving time.
Food only: a smoker cannot smelt ores, stone, sand or anything that is not food. Its mirror twin, the blast furnace, does ores and metal gear at double speed instead.
Use it in villages: smokers generate naturally in butcher houses, and placing one near an unemployed villager turns them into a butcher - your source for cooked meat trades and emeralds.
Automate it: hoppers can load raw food on top, fuel on the side, and pull cooked food from the bottom - and a lit smoker emits light level 13 while working.
editionNote: Identical recipe and speed in both editions. The version paths differed: Java got smokers fully in 1.14, while Bedrock added them in 1.9.0 behind Experimental Gameplay and only made them functional in 1.11.0.
versions: Smokers were added in Java 1.14 (snapshot 18w44a) and Bedrock 1.9.0 (experimental; functional from 1.11.0).

faq.q: What is the point of a smoker in Minecraft?
faq.a: Speed. It cooks food twice as fast as a furnace (5 seconds per item) at the same fuel efficiency per item. For bulk steak, baked potatoes or dried kelp, a smoker halves your waiting.

faq.q: Smoker vs blast furnace - which do I need?
faq.a: Both, ideally. The smoker only cooks food; the blast furnace only smelts ores, raw metals and metal tools/armor - each at double speed. A regular furnace does everything slowly.

faq.q: Why is my villager not taking the smoker job?
faq.a: The villager must be unemployed (not a nitwit), able to pathfind to the smoker, and it must be during work hours. Break other nearby job site blocks first - villagers claim the closest valid one.

keywords: smoker minecraft craft furnace 4 logs cook food twice as fast butcher job site blast furnace vs smoker

name: How to Make a Boat in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a boat with 5 matching planks in a U shape. Place it on water and right-click to ride - boats are the fastest cheap travel in the game, fly across ice, and even trap mobs that walk into them.
steps: Chop any overworld tree and craft 5 matching planks - all 5 must be the same wood type. Oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, bamboo (makes a raft), pale oak and crimson... no wait, crimson and warped are Nether fungi and cannot make boats.
Craft it: planks in the middle-left and middle-right, and a full bottom row - a U shape.
Place the boat on water and use it to hop in. Steer with your movement keys; no fuel, no paddles needed in modern versions.
Break it to pick it back up: one hit and it drops as an item. Boats are also perfect one-way tickets - mobs that wander into a boat cannot get out, so park one next to a zombie and it is yours.
Ride ice highways: boats slide at extreme speed on ice, packed ice and especially blue ice - the fastest overland travel in the game without elytra.
Add a chest: combine the boat with a chest for a boat with chest, floating storage for long trips.
Bring friends: a boat fits two entities - you plus a villager, an animal, or a friend. Boats are THE way to kidnap villagers for a trading hall.
Fall safely: in Java, boats negate fall damage entirely when you land in one - MLG boat clutches are a thing.
materials: 5 matching planks of one overworld wood
editionNote: Same recipe in both editions (the old Pocket Edition recipe with a wooden shovel is long gone). Control feel differs slightly between editions, and Java's boats fully cancel fall damage - Bedrock players still take the hit if the boat lands on land.
versions: Boats were added in Java Alpha v1.0.6 - one of the oldest vehicles in gaming - and in Pocket Edition 0.11.0. The one-wood-type-per-boat variants and the chest boat arrived much later (1.9 and 1.19).

faq.q: Why can't I craft a bamboo boat?
faq.a: Bamboo works differently: 5 bamboo planks make a bamboo raft, which works exactly like a boat. Nether woods (crimson, warped) cannot be made into boats at all.

faq.q: How do you transport villagers in Minecraft?
faq.a: Push a boat into them or place it right next to them and they climb in - then row them anywhere. Combine with rails for the classic villager moving service.

faq.q: Is a boat faster than a horse?
faq.a: On water, absolutely. On blue ice a boat hits extreme speeds - over 70 blocks per second - faster than almost anything except elytra with rockets.

keywords: boat minecraft craft 5 planks ride water ice blue ice fast travel villager transport boat with chest raft

name: How to Make a Grindstone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a grindstone with 2 sticks, 1 stone slab and 2 planks. It removes enchantments from items (refunding some XP) and repairs gear by combining two damaged pieces - no levels needed.
steps: Get 2 sticks (2 planks), 2 planks of any wood, and 1 stone slab (smelt cobblestone into stone, then 3 stone = 6 slabs).
Craft it: sticks in the top corners, the stone slab between them on top, and one plank below each stick.

Disenchant anything: put an enchanted item in the grindstone and take out the clean item - every enchantment comes off (except curses like Curse of Binding) and you get some XP back based on the enchantments removed.
Clean up junk loot: grind off the bad enchantments from fishing loot, raid drops and skeleton gear before combining or re-enchanting. Enchanted books cannot be disenchanted, though.
Repair without an anvil: two damaged items of the same type combine into one with their durability added together plus a 5% bonus - free, no XP cost, but any enchantments are wiped.
Know the trade-off vs the anvil: the anvil keeps and combines enchantments for levels; the grindstone removes them for free. Different tools for different jobs.
Use it in villages: grindstones generate in weaponsmith houses, and placing one turns an unemployed villager into a weaponsmith - swords and axes for emeralds.
editionNote: Identical in both editions. The XP refund from disenchanting scales with the enchantments removed, so grinding a maxed-out fishing rod is a nice little XP snack.
versions: Grindstones were added in Java 1.14 (snapshot 18w44a) and Bedrock 1.9.0 behind Experimental Gameplay; they became functional in Bedrock 1.11.0.

faq.q: Does a grindstone give you XP back?
faq.a: Yes - disenchanting an item refunds experience based on the enchantments it had. It is never the full enchanting cost, but stripping enchanted fishing loot adds up fast.

faq.q: Grindstone vs anvil - which should I use?
faq.a: Grindstone to REMOVE enchantments (free, refunds some XP, destroys the enchants) or to merge durability cheaply. Anvil to KEEP and combine enchantments, rename, or repair with materials - for levels.

faq.q: Can a grindstone remove curses?
faq.a: No. Curse of Binding and Curse of Vanishing survive the grindstone. Only dying or creative mode removes a cursed item you are stuck wearing.

keywords: grindstone minecraft craft 2 sticks stone slab planks remove enchantments disenchant refund xp repair vs anvil weaponsmith

name: How to Make a Crossbow in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a crossbow with 3 sticks, 2 string, 1 iron ingot and 1 tripwire hook. It loads an arrow you can hold ready indefinitely, fires fireworks as rockets, and gets exclusive enchantments: Quick Charge, Multishot and Piercing.
steps: Get 3 sticks, 2 string (spiders or cobwebs), 1 iron ingot and 1 tripwire hook (iron ingot + stick + plank).
Craft it: sticks top corners, iron ingot top-center, string on both middle sides, tripwire hook in the very center, stick bottom-center.
Load and hold: use the crossbow once to load an arrow - it stays loaded forever until you fire, even in your inventory. Pre-load several crossbows for an instant volley.
Fire it: use again to shoot. Base damage is high (6-11), it charges in 1.25 seconds, and arrows fly further and flatter than a bow's.
Shoot fireworks: put a firework rocket in your off-hand and load it - the rocket flies straight and explodes on impact for area damage. Each rocket costs 3 durability.

Enchant it: Quick Charge III drops reload to 0.5 seconds, Multishot fires 3 arrows at once for the price of 1, and Piercing IV shoots through up to 5 entities and ignores shields. Multishot and Piercing are mutually exclusive.
Loot one instead: pillagers drop crossbows 8.5% of the time (+1% per Looting level), sometimes enchanted; piglins can spawn with them too.
Mind the durability: 465 shots in Java, 466 in Bedrock. Repair on an anvil or with Mending - piercing crossbows make arrow farms nearly free since the arrow drops after passing through.
editionNote: Mechanics match across editions, with two Java-only touches: fireworks explode on contact with blocks and entities (in Bedrock they pass through and explode at the end), and the 'ding' hit sound is Java-only.
versions: Crossbows were added in Java 1.14 (snapshot 18w43a) and Bedrock 1.8.0 behind Experimental Gameplay.

faq.q: Crossbow or bow - which is better?
faq.a: Bow for sustained fire and Infinity; crossbow for burst damage, pre-loaded shots and fireworks. Quick Charge III makes the crossbow nearly as fast, and Multishot shreds groups at close range.

faq.q: Can a crossbow shoot fireworks?
faq.a: Yes: hold a firework rocket in your off-hand while loading. The rocket flies straight, explodes on impact (Java) and deals area damage that scales with the number of firework stars. Multishot fires three rockets at once.

faq.q: What enchantments can a crossbow have?
faq.a: Quick Charge (faster reload), Multishot (3 projectiles per shot), Piercing (arrows pass through entities and shields), plus Unbreaking and Mending. Multishot and Piercing exclude each other, and it cannot have Power or Infinity.

keywords: crossbow minecraft craft 3 sticks 2 string iron tripwire hook quick charge multishot piercing fireworks vs bow pillager drop

name: How to Make Bread in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft bread with 3 wheat in a row. It restores 5 hunger points, stacks to 64, and doubles as villager currency - farmers buy wheat, and bread makes villagers willing to breed.
steps: Get wheat: break tall grass for seeds, hoe dirt near water, plant them and wait through 8 growth stages - or raid village farms, which are full of ready wheat.
Speed it up: bone meal (from skeleton bones) grows wheat instantly; hydrated farmland within 4 blocks of water grows fastest.
Craft bread: 3 wheat in a horizontal row. One craft, one bread.
Eat it: restores 5 hunger points (2.5 shanks) with modest saturation. Not the best food late game, but the first reliable one most players ever get.
Loot it too: bread shows up in village, dungeon, mineshaft, stronghold and woodland mansion chests, and farmer villagers throw it at you if you have Hero of the Village.
Breed villagers with it: toss 3 bread at a villager (12 for full willingness) and they become willing to breed - bread is the engine of every villager breeder.
Trade the wheat instead: farmer villagers buy 20 wheat for an emerald, so a wheat farm feeds both you and your emerald supply.
Automate it: farmers harvest and craft bread themselves, then share it - an automatic potato/carrot-free bread factory is just two farmers and some farmland.
editionNote: Identical in both editions. The hunger and saturation values match exactly; the only difference is how fast crops tick in each edition's random tick system.
versions: Bread was added in Java Indev on February 6, 2010 - one of the game's first foods - and in Pocket Edition 0.4.0.

faq.q: How do you get wheat in Minecraft?
faq.a: Plant seeds (from breaking tall grass) on hoed farmland and wait, or harvest the wheat fields that generate in villages. Bone meal ripens crops instantly.

faq.q: How much hunger does bread restore?
faq.a: 5 hunger points (2.5 drumsticks) per loaf. Steak and cooked porkchops beat it at 8, but bread is far easier to mass-produce early on.

faq.q: Why do I need bread for villagers?
faq.a: Villagers only breed when willing, and food creates willingness: 3 bread (or 12 carrots/potatoes/beetroots) per villager. Throw it at them and let the farmer do the farming.

name: How to Make a Cake in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a cake with 3 milk buckets on top, sugar-egg-sugar in the middle and 3 wheat on the bottom. Place it down and eat 7 slices worth 14 hunger total - the most hunger of any single food item, and yes, the cake is a lie.
steps: Get 3 milk buckets: craft 3 buckets (9 iron) and right-click cows, mooshrooms or goats. The buckets come back after crafting.
Get 2 sugar: craft sugar cane (found on riverbanks and beaches) into sugar.
Get 1 egg: chickens lay one every 5-10 minutes, so pen a few up - any egg type works.
Get 3 wheat: grow it from seeds on farmland or steal it from village fields.
Craft the cake: milk buckets filling the top row, sugar-egg-sugar in the middle row, wheat filling the bottom row.
Place it to eat: cake is a block, not a snack - it does nothing from your hand. Put it down and use it; each use eats one of its 7 slices, 2 hunger each, 14 hunger for the whole cake.
Know the quirks: once placed, a cake can never be picked up again (not even with Silk Touch). Eating is instant - no eating animation - so it is great panic food mid-fight.
Party tricks: put a candle on it for a birthday cake (since 1.17), feed slices to pandas, or read the remaining slices with a comparator for redstone builds.
editionNote: Identical in both editions, candles included. The whole-cake 14 hunger points is the highest of any food in the game - but the saturation is low, so you get hungry again fast.
versions: Cake was added in Java Beta 1.2 after Minecraft won the 2010 Indie of the Year award, with the famous 'The Lie' achievement (a Portal reference) arriving in 1.5; Pocket Edition got it in 0.7.0.

faq.q: Why can't I eat my cake?
faq.a: Cake must be placed as a block first - you cannot eat it from your hand. Once placed, it cannot be picked back up, so choose the spot wisely.

faq.q: How many slices does a Minecraft cake have?
faq.a: Seven. Each slice restores 2 hunger points, so a whole cake is 14 hunger - the most of any food item - but with very low saturation.

faq.q: How do you put a candle on a cake?
faq.a: Hold any candle and use it on a placed cake. Light it with flint and steel for a birthday cake. Breaking the cake drops nothing, so eat it first.

name: How to Make a Minecart in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a minecart with 5 iron ingots in a U shape. Place it on rails to ride at up to 8 blocks per second - faster with powered rails - and haul villagers, mobs and chests across your world.
steps: Smelt 5 iron ingots (iron ore is everywhere; bring a stone pickaxe or better).
Craft it: ingots in the middle-left, middle-right and the full bottom row - a U shape, like the bucket recipe with 2 extra ingots.
Lay rails: craft 16 rails from 6 iron + 1 stick, and powered rails from 6 gold + stick + redstone. A minecart is useless without a track.
Ride it: place the minecart on a rail and use it to hop in. It hits its 8 blocks/second top speed on flat powered rails and coasts downhill for free.
Boost with powered rails: an unpowered powered rail is a brake, a lit one is a booster. One powered rail every ~38 blocks keeps top speed on flat ground.
Move mobs and villagers: push a mob into a minecart and it cannot leave - the safest way to ship villagers to a trading hall or a zombie to your base.
Make the variants: combine with a chest, hopper, TNT or furnace for the chest, hopper, TNT and furnace minecarts - mobile storage, item collection, bombs and self-propulsion.
Loot them instead: mineshaft chests contain minecarts and rails in bulk - bring a stack of torches and rob an abandoned mineshaft instead of crafting.
materials: Plus rails: 6 iron + 1 stick = 16 rails; powered rails need 6 gold + stick + redstone dust
editionNote: Identical in both editions. The classic legacy-console trick of 16 blocks/second minecarts never existed in Java or Bedrock - 8 m/s is the cap on powered rails.
versions: Minecarts were added in Java Infdev on June 18, 2010 - the update literally named after their 'infinite development' potential - and in Pocket Edition 0.8.0.

faq.q: How do you make a minecart go faster?
faq.a: Powered rails. Place them every 30-40 blocks on flat ground (more uphill), power them with a redstone torch or lever, and the minecart holds its 8 blocks/second top speed.

faq.q: How do you transport villagers with a minecart?
faq.a: Build rails to the villager, push a minecart into them (they board automatically when it touches them), and send it off. Boats work too and need no rails.

faq.q: Minecart or boat - which is better for transport?
faq.a: Boats are cheaper and work anywhere with water or ice; minecarts shine for automated stations, item transport with hopper minecarts, and moving mobs uphill where boats cannot go.

keywords: minecart minecraft craft 5 iron ingots rails powered rail speed 8 blocks per second villager transport mineshaft

name: How to Make a Dispenser in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a dispenser with 7 cobblestone, 1 bow and 1 redstone dust. Power it with redstone and it fires or uses a random item from its 9 slots - arrows, water buckets, shears, bonemeal - the heart of every automatic farm.
steps: Mine 7 cobblestone, get 1 redstone dust (deep ore, iron pickaxe+) and craft or loot 1 bow (3 sticks + 3 string - a damaged bow works too).
Craft it: cobblestone filling everything except the center, where the bow goes, and the bottom-center, where the redstone dust goes.
Fill its 9 slots and power it: every redstone pulse dispenses ONE randomly chosen item. It does not pick in order, so keep item types separated.
Weaponize it: arrows, fire charges, splash potions, tridents and fireworks shoot out as projectiles - instant traps and defenses.
Automate fluids: a dispenser with a water or lava bucket places the fluid on the first pulse and sucks it back up on the next - perfect flushers for crop farms and mob farms.
Automate tools: shears shear sheep and harvest honeycomb, flint and steel lights TNT and campfires, bonemeal grows crops, and empty bottles scoop honey - almost every use-item action works.
Equip and place: dispensers put armor and carved pumpkins on players and mobs, place shulker boxes, boats and minecarts, and spawn mobs from spawn eggs.
Power it smartly: a dispenser needs a pulse edge (button, observer clock, pressure plate). An observer watching a comparator or a simple repeater loop is the classic farm clock.
editionNote: Nearly identical in both editions; some edge behaviors differ (Bedrock dispensers can suck honey into bottles from hives with slightly different timing). The random slot choice is the same everywhere - design around it.
versions: Dispensers were added in Java Beta 1.2 and Pocket Edition 0.14.0, the big redstone update for mobile.

faq.q: What is the difference between a dropper and a dispenser?
faq.a: A dropper just ejects the item as an item (or pushes it into a container). A dispenser USES the item: shoots arrows, places water, shears sheep, equips armor. For storage systems you want droppers; for farms and traps, dispensers.

faq.q: How do you power a dispenser automatically?
faq.a: Give it repeated redstone pulses: an observer facing another observer makes a fast clock, a hopper clock is slower and cheaper, and a lever or button works for single shots.

faq.q: Can a dispenser place blocks?
faq.a: Only specific ones: shulker boxes, boats, minecarts, armor stands, carved pumpkins and heads on armor stands/mobs. For normal blocks you need a different trick - pistons or the player.

keywords: dispenser minecraft craft 7 cobblestone bow redstone automatic farm arrows water bucket shear sheep dropper vs dispenser

name: How to Make a Ladder in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft 3 ladders with 7 sticks in an H shape. Stick them to walls to climb straight up - no jumping needed - and they even hold back water and lava while letting you breathe.
steps: Craft sticks: 2 planks = 4 sticks. You need 7 sticks per craft.
Craft ladders: sticks in an H - both side columns full and one in the center. Each craft gives 3 ladders.
Place them against the side of any solid block and walk into them to climb up or down - no jump key required.
Descend safely: hold sneak while on a ladder and you stop in place - perfect for building off the side of a cliff or a tall tower.

Beat the physics: ladders displace water and lava to create an air pocket, so a ladder column is an underwater breathing shaft. In a water source block the ladder becomes waterlogged instead and gives no air.
Light ceilings with lava: a ladder in a block below lava stops it dripping through while the glow still shines down - the classic lava ceiling trick.

Use them as cheap scaffolding: ladders stick to walls at any height, mobs can technically climb them but almost never pathfind onto them, and you can skip every other ladder to save sticks if your aim is good.
Alternatives when you outgrow them: vines (free, but you need shears), scaffolding (bamboo + string, buildable from the bottom) and bubble elevators (soul sand/magma in water).
editionNote: Identical climbing in both editions. The waterlogged behavior matches too: inside a water source the ladder floods and gives no air pocket, in flowing water it stays dry.
versions: Ladders were added to Java in Infdev on June 7, 2010 - Notch famously said ladders are never fun, but fans convinced him - and have been in Pocket Edition since its demo.

faq.q: How many ladders do you get from one craft?
faq.a: Three ladders from 7 sticks. A stick is half a plank, so one ladder costs roughly 1.2 planks - very cheap vertical travel.

faq.q: Can mobs climb ladders?
faq.a: Technically yes - their pathfinding can push them up - but they almost never climb on purpose. A ladder does not make your base less safe, though a staircase of any kind is an open invitation.

faq.q: How do you breathe underwater with a ladder?
faq.a: Place a ladder on a wall underwater (in flowing water or against a block, not inside a source block) and it keeps an air pocket around itself - stand in it to refill your bubbles.

keywords: ladder minecraft craft 7 sticks 3 ladders climb walls underwater air pocket lava ceiling scaffolding alternative

name: How to Make Flint and Steel in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft flint and steel with 1 iron ingot and 1 flint (from gravel) anywhere in the grid. It sets fires, lights Nether portals, ignites TNT and creepers, and relights campfires and candles.
steps: Get flint: mine gravel - each block has a 10% chance to drop flint instead of gravel (Fortune raises it, Fortune III guarantees it). Gravel is everywhere: caves, rivers, ocean floors, the Nether.
Smelt 1 iron ingot.
Craft it: iron ingot and flint anywhere in the crafting grid - it is shapeless.
Light a Nether portal: use it inside an obsidian frame and the fire becomes portal blocks. This is THE way to light portals - always carry one in the Nether in case a ghast de-lights your way home.
Detonate on demand: use it on TNT to prime it, or right-click a creeper to force it to explode where it stands - a genuinely useful combat trick.
Relight everything: campfires, candles, candle cakes and fireplaces all relight with a click. Fire spreads on flammable blocks, so mind your wooden roof.
Repair and enchant: combine two worn ones in a grid, or add Unbreaking/Mending. It has 64 uses in Java, 65 in Bedrock.
Find one instead: ruined portal chests and some dungeon chests contain flint and steel - check the next ruined portal you pass.
materials: 1 flint (10% drop from gravel, guaranteed with Fortune III)
editionNote: Identical in both editions apart from the one-point durability difference (64 Java, 65 Bedrock). Fire spread rules differ slightly between editions, so a fire that burns out in Java may keep going in Bedrock - and vice versa with rain.
versions: Flint and steel was added to Java in Indev 0.31 on January 10, 2010 - originally with infinite uses - and to Pocket Edition 0.4.0.

faq.q: How do you get flint in Minecraft?
faq.a: Mine gravel: each block has a 10% chance to drop flint instead of itself. Re-place and re-mine the gravel you get, or use a Fortune III shovel for guaranteed flint every block.

faq.q: How do you light a Nether portal without flint and steel?
faq.a: Fire charges (dispensable too), lava dripping fire onto wood inside the frame, or a ghast fireball all light portals. But flint and steel is the only reliable pocket option.

faq.q: Can flint and steel light an End portal?
faq.a: No. End portal frames only activate with eyes of ender - no fire needed. Flint and steel lights Nether portals, TNT, creepers, campfires, candles and plain fires.
